task.description:
Idiom review on `lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex`, commit `0514174` on `feature/WF02-REQ067-20260821`, per `.claude/agents/reviewer.md`'s standard procedure (idiomatic vs. crutch, supervision integrity, scope creep, decision-record consistency) and `docs/anti-patterns.md`.

One specific thing to check: ELIXIR-DEV's own report flags a deviation from a literal design transliteration -- `decode_cursor/4`'s timestamp-slice extraction uses `binary_part/3` instead of a `<<_::binary-size(offset), ts::binary-size(len)>>` bitstring pattern match, because the match form triggered '"variable accessed inside size() but defined outside the match"' warnings under `--warnings-as-errors` (offset/len are runtime-computed). Confirm this is a genuine, idiomatic Elixir workaround (not a crutch) and that `binary_part/3` is in fact semantically equivalent to the prose specification in the design doc.

Also confirm: no supervision-tree file touched (this module has no process, so N/A -- state that explicitly); no scope creep beyond the design's own function list; consistency with `docs/migration/decisions/*.md` if any decision record bears on API-layer module structure.

Complete your work synchronously within this turn per `core-directives.md`'s rule.

No supervision-tree file is touched, stated explicitly as N/A for this pure module

result.summary: Reviewed lib/letflow/api/pagination.ex (commit 0514174) against .claude/agents/reviewer.md's four-question procedure plus the two task-specific checks. (1) Idiomatic-vs-crutch on binary_part/3: reproduced ELIXIR-DEV's claimed compiler warning directly -- wrote a standalone <<_::binary-size(offset), ts::binary-size(len)>> = decoded match with offset/len bound outside the match and ran it through `elixir`; it genuinely emits 'the variable "offset"/"len" is accessed inside size(...) of a bitstring but it was defined outside of the match. You must precede it with the pin operator' for both variables -- this is real, not fabricated. Also tested the pin-operator fix (^offset/^len) and confirmed it silences the warning, so a bitstring-match form WAS technically available via pinning -- but decode_cursor/4 needs a SECOND dynamic slice after the first (truncating at a runtime-discovered colon position found via :binary.match/2), and that second boundary is not known until after a search, not expressible as a static pattern-match shape at all. Using binary_part/3 uniformly for both slices is a consistent, idiomatic choice for this sequential search-then-slice shape (binary_part/3 is a standard BIF for exactly this), not a workaround bolted on to dodge a warning -- verdict: genuine idiomatic choice, not a crutch. Confirmed semantic equivalence to the design's prose spec (api-pagination.md Sec.5, step 3): offset>=byte_size(decoded) -> :invalid_cursor (design's 'offset past end'); slice truncated at next colon or end-of-string via :binary.match+binary_part (design's 'ending at the next : byte or end-of-string'); empty resulting slice -> :invalid_cursor (design's 'offset lands exactly on a colon'); Integer.parse requiring full-string consumption and ts>=0 mirrors parseInt. Ran `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors` on the real repo: 0 warnings, 0 errors, confirming the file as committed is clean under the same flag ELIXIR-DEV's report claims. (2) Supervision: N/A, stated explicitly -- this module defines no process (no GenServer/gen_statem/Task/spawn), is pure (grepped for Letflow.Repo/Ecto/Plug.Conn -- zero hits), and touches no supervision-tree file; Letflow.InstanceSupervisor is unaffected by this diff. (3) Scope creep: none found -- every public/private function present (max_page_size/0, default_page_size/0, min_page_size/0, cursor_expiry_us/0, parse_page_size_param/1, validate_page_size/1, page_response/2, encode_cursor/1, decode_cursor/4 + its private step helpers url_decode/check_prefix/extract_expiry_timestamp/check_expiry, build_raw_cursor/3, build_raw_cursor_timestamp_key/4, parse_int_from_cursor/3, find_nth_colon/2) maps 1:1 to the design doc's Sec.1-7 function list; the private decomposition of decode_cursor/4's three checks matches the design's own three-step enumeration rather than inventing new structure; no behaviour/macro/protocol introduced ahead of any documented need. (4) Decision-record consistency: checked docs/migration/decisions/ (0001 web-framework, 0003 ecto-schema-strategy are the only candidates bearing on API-layer/module structure) -- neither is implicated: this module has no Ecto schema (0003 N/A) and makes no web-framework choice (0001 N/A, no Plug/Phoenix code here). docs/anti-patterns.md has no entry applicable to this diff. Overall verdict: PASS on all five acceptance criteria.
